> Aussiefied at **Swaggie** level, with **Dinkum** embellishment and **Dad** vulgarity. [Prefer docs that are as dry as a dead dingo's donger?](../plain/functional/toolkit.md)

# The toolkit and its surfaces

Language models are good at Australian English when they have quality source material'n clear guidance.
So anyway, the toolkit gives them both, as plain functions that return JSON\-ready dicts. `aussiefy.harness` gathers
them; `lookup`, `lint` and `guide` each live in their own module \(`lookup.py`, `lint.py`, `guide.py`).

| Function | CLI | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `bulldust(concept)` | `aussiefy bulldust HUNGRY` | Seeded idiom construction from reviewed families, labelled bulldust with evidence on every part; [reference](bulldust.md) |
| `list_entries`, `get_entry`, `random_entry`, `list_wordless_meanings`, `suggest_name`, `variations` | `entries`, `entry`, `random-entry`, `wordless-meanings`, `suggest-name`, `variations` | [Dictionary exploration](exploring.md), meanings without a word yet, clean handles and construction variations |
| `lookup(query)` | `aussiefy lookup "very busy"` | Genuine Aussie options for a meaning, or what a term means ("goog"), filtered to the level and vulgarity |
| `lint(text)` | `aussiefy lint < draft.txt` | Lints a draft for flagged non-Aussie phrases, swearing over the cap (via `aussiefy/data/swears.yaml`), US spelling and US/UK words (`aussiefy/data/dialect.yaml`), plus optional "could be more Aussie" suggestions. With `original=`, also checks fidelity: length, and names and numbers kept or invented |
| `guide(level)` | `aussiefy guide -l 5` | Voice, language limits and the craft rules learned from good translations (swear inside sentences, tag-ons only in dialogue, connectives in narration, no pile-ups, Australian spelling); craft is filtered to the requested dials; `aussiefy/data/guide.yaml` also owns the workflow, plan note and yarn rules |
| `plan(text)` | `aussiefy plan < in.txt` | The engine's draft, its planned phrases, riffs and suggested openings, and the sentences it found too formal |
| `translate(text)` | `aussiefy "text"` | The deterministic rule-engine output |
| `verify(text, original=...)` | `aussiefy verify draft.txt --original original.txt` | Severity-based fidelity, structure and policy checks; [reference](verification.md) |

Well, how an agent uses them, step by step, is in [skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md](../../skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md),
which also explains each kind of lint issue \(`!`), warnin' \(`?`) and suggestion \(`~`).

## The Python API

```python
from aussiefy import Translator, translate, lookup, lint, guide, plan, yarn, load_dictionary

r = translate("I'm extremely busy.", level=4, seed=7)
r.text          # "I'm flat out like a lizard drinking."
r.decisions()   # spans, chosen entries and garnish: what the engine decided
r.to_dict()     # the policy envelope, decisions, explain records and difficult_sentences

tr = Translator()   # reuse for many calls; Translator(load_dictionary(["my-extra.yaml"])) to extend
tr.translate(text, level="swaggie", seed=1, vulgarity="dad", regions=["vic"], unlock=["archaic"])
lookup("very tired", translator=tr)   # the toolkit functions take a translator too; the default is shared
```

`translate_changes` takes `translate`'s parameters, plus `embedder` (the similarity fallback), and returns a
`ChangeSet`: the same translation, with every change it made and each swap's alternatives rendered in place
([changes](changes.md)). It's for a host that lets a reader edit a translation, so it's in the Python API only, not
the CLI, MCP tools or yarn mode. `aussiefy.guide.dial_descriptions()` lists every setting of the level, vulgarity
and embellishment dials and every document type, each with a one-line description from `aussiefy/data/guide.yaml`.

Except for clean name suggestions, toolkit operations take keyword-only dials, by number or name: `level` (default 5) and `vulgarity` (default: the
level's own). `translate`, `plan`, `yarn` and `bulldust` also take `seed` (default 0). `translate` and `plan` also take
`variety`; they and `bulldust` take `registers`, `regions` and `unlock`; only `translate` takes `markdown` (default false).
The core engine/Translator consumes plain text or internally masked text. `translate`, `plan`, `lint`, `verify`
and `yarn` support the extended `markup` route; strict `markdown=True` source units belong only to translation.
`lookup` takes `limit` (default 8) and `include_gated`; `lint` takes `original`. Every function takes an optional
`translator` for a non-default dictionary.

Document operations (`translate`, `plan`, `lint`, `verify`, `guide`, `yarn`, `bulldust`) also take `document_type="general"`
and `document_config=None`, plus the `embellishment` dial (0–2 or its name; omitted uses the selected preset).
General defaults to Dinkum; Auto opts into detection; named types select presets;
Custom enables only configured optional behaviours. The shared override object replaces inherited values after
explicit dials, including false and empty lists. See [translation controls](translation-controls.md).
Its nested `profile` tunes engine rates, limits, spacing, frames, drawl, swearing and rewrite thresholds.
Partial maps inherit missing keys. Every document operation's result includes the resolved `profile_config`
(lookup omits the numeric profile snapshot); document operations accept that snapshot back as `document_config.profile`. Custom still needs optional document
behaviours enabled explicitly, even when their numeric settings are supplied.

`translate` returns a `Result`, or `DocumentResult` with explicit `markdown=True`
([Markdown contract](markdown.md)); the other toolkit functions return dicts, and `yarn` returns a result whose
`outcome` is `applied` or `fell_back`. The package also exports `Policy`, `Dictionary`, `Entry`,
`default_translator`, and the two errors it raises on purpose: `SchemaError` (an invalid dictionary) and
`UserError` (a problem the user can fix; the CLI prints it and exits 2).

`Result.to_dict()` is a superset of the toolkit translate dict: `text`, `level`, `level_name`, `vulgarity`,
`vulgarity_name`, `policy_warnings`, `profile_config`, `seed`, `variety`, `decisions` and `difficult_sentences`, plus `source`
and `explain`. V3 also includes `dictionary_id`, `card_version`, `tuning`, `warnings` and `warning_details`. The old `difficult` key is gone; `policy_warnings` remains for compatibility. Policy warnings name region
tags or unlock flags unused by the dictionary; invalid register and unlock names raise `UserError`.

`themes=None` and `invention=None` are top-level document controls. Exact theme overrides merge per
key over `document_config.themes`; an explicit top-level invention boolean wins over the document
override. Every document type accepts the switch. Troppo enables invention by default, Dinkum and
Deadset leave it off, and Custom requires an explicit permission. Translation tries a bounded
reviewed construction only when no curated candidate fits, before the substitution roll; a failed
curated roll never triggers invention. Shared slot, frame, degree, article and protection checks apply.
Unsupported construction frames and dependent result clauses stay plain. Constructed openers also
obey the switch; ordinary garnish, entry riffs and contextual imagery keep their own permissions.

`translate` and plans take `popularity=False`, `preferences=None` and `pins=None`.
Python preferences are a latest\-first list of `{match, term, weight}`, with finite weights at least
1. Exact keys win over the first same\-root preference. Unknown matches/terms warn with stable
codes; the public tunin' summary reports popularity'n the number of distinct preference records
actually used. Now, preferences change weights before variety, retain repeats'n failed rolls, and
never change eligibility or evidence. [Replay pins](changes.md#explicit-replay-pins) retain choices
when tunin' is removed. Yarn accepts popularity/preferences'n uses the same plan boundary.

Plans label constructed choices with null `entry`, a `construction_id`, local part provenance,
canonical construction cards and a shared `scaffold`. The standalone constructor and Yarn expose
the same reviewed meanings, examples, families, typed ingredients, stems, endings and constraints.
An agent's new wording is bulldust made by the agent, never a claim of attestation. Yarn explicitly
allows misreadable terms across its plan, lookup, lint and validation; other gates still apply.
Standalone lookup/lint/verify accept the same optional `unlock` permission.

Struth, MCP tools expose parameter descriptions'n dial choices in their schemas, and preserve `UserError`
messages as tool errors. `lookup` requires `limit >= 1` and marks each riff's `best` fit.

A hosted MCP server narrows the tools by capability ([DD-028](../architecture/decisions/dd-028-hosted-mcp-capabilities.md)).
`build_server(translator=…, allow_unlock=False, allow_include_gated=False, allow_document_config=False, max_chars=…, max_query_chars=…,
lookup_limit=…)` independently hides translation's `unlock` and discovery's `include_gated`, hides `document_config` and the `custom` document type,
caps `text` and `original`, and caps lookup's `query` and `limit`, along with entry-page sizes. Bulldust advertises `1 <= limit <= min(max_results, lookup_limit)`
(or the loaded constructor maximum without a host cap), with a default that fits. Over-limit calls fail schema validation before entering the toolkit. The defaults serve everything. Every tool is annotated read-only,
non-destructive, idempotent and closed-world.
`allow_include_gated` defaults to true even when `allow_unlock` is false, so a host can show held-back
terms with their provenance without unlocking automatic translations. Hidden options keep their closed
defaults even when sent anyway. Lookup's limit also caps cited word cards per ruled-out meaning.

`build_server` additionally accepts `allow_tuning`, `allow_themes`, `allow_invention` (all true by
default), `preferences_hook=None` and `tools=None`. The tool allowlist uses canonical names and
rejects unknown names. Hiding document configuration does not hide the two independent permission
controls. Disabling a capability removes it from schemas; the MCP adapter ignores unknown top-level
arguments, so hidden values keep their closed defaults. Attempts to bypass disabled theme/invention
permissions through document configuration fail. `allow_tuning` controls popularity only: hosted clients never send
raw personal preferences. The synchronous host hook runs once per request, including whole Markdown
documents, with resolved numeric keyword dials `level`, `vulgarity`, `embellishment`. It returns the
latest-first records for that call, or None. Host identity stays in the host's context; the package
never knows whose preferences they are. The hook remains usable when popularity is hidden.

## The same toolkit, three more ways

- **MCP server, for any MCP-capable agent.** The `aussiefy-mcp` command (stdio) serves the tools
  `aussie_lookup`, `aussie_lint`, `aussie_guide`, `aussie_plan`, `aussie_translate`, `aussie_verify` and `aussie_bulldust`, plus the [exploration tools](exploring.md). Setup is in the
  [user guide](../user/agents.md).
- **Portable CLI skill.** [skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md](../../skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md) walks an agent through
  brief → guide → plan → write with lookups → lint'n fix → verify → deliver, using the CLI.
- **Shared retelling session.** `aussiefy.retelling` owns `brief()`, `dispatch_tool()` and `tool_contracts()`:
  model-independent briefs, checked tool calls and neutral JSON Schemas for `lookup`, `lint` and `submit`.
  Clients adapt those contracts to their own transport. The optional `aussiefy.yarn` API driver derives its
  Anthropic `tool_definitions()` from them. Existing `from aussiefy.yarn import brief, dispatch_tool` imports
  remain supported. On the package, `aussiefy.yarn` is the convenience function, not the module.

Every surface takes the same parameters by the same names and defaults; `tests/functional/test_interfaces.py` holds them
in step (see [DD-008](../architecture/decisions/dd-008-one-toolkit-thin-surfaces.md)).

Genre, English, embellishment'n extended document controls are described in [translation controls](translation-controls.md).
Lookup's full cards share the discovery builder in `aussiefy/cards.py`, including structured sources,
attestation, evidence'n tag placement. Changes\-v2 cards retain their existin' representation until the
coordinated contract bump. `lookup(short=True)` offers compact cards with match\-kind codes;
`lint(suggest=False)` skips optional engine suggestions. Lookup also reports the dictionary identity and
structured preservation outcomes; see [exploration contracts](exploring.md#outcomes).

## Lookup sense matching

`validate_source_url(url)` is an exported Python helper for citation links. It returns the unchanged URL
or raises `UserError`. It checks HTTP(S), public hostname syntax, the 2048-character limit, and rejects
credentials, IP literals, non-default ports, spaces and controls. It performs no fetch or DNS resolution
and does not certify the cited content. Dictionary citation loading uses the same check.

Lookup matches complete slang forms with grammatical slots, so “give them a bell” reaches the telephone
sense. Crikey, complete form, inflected form'n partial\-term discovery explain vocabulary broadly; their cards
don't promise an in\-place replacement for the query. Inflection applies to a noun's head or a verb
phrase's head verb, not every word of every frame: “shouted” doesn't become a drinks noun.

Meaning inference shares canonical source concepts, polarity, argument restrictions'n reviewed degree
certificates. Bloody hell, a recognised query head can exclude unrelated suggestions; “probably” doesn't establish
certainty, “wake up” doesn't establish hurrying, and a beer can is distinct from a small bottle. The
dictionary can recognise a meaning without having a compatible target, and then explains that abstention.
Mind ya, explicit mild/strong source degree needs a compatible certified target for an inferred meaning match.

Local readings aren't a whole\-query parse. Attributive'n coordinated query fragments retain their
meanings, while unknown modifiers, subordinate content'n unresolved structure leave model fallback
available. External negation is checked before a source phrase, preservin' established internally negative
meanings such as “not bad” and “not working”. Stone the crows, an independently supported positive sense can keep on kickin' another
sense's denial; an unrelated label can't rescue a denied meaning. Well, lexical ranking'n model texts use the
same permitted paths. Negated model fallback also needs a shared content anchor with candidate wording.

These are bounded checks, not a general word\-sense classifier. Mate, explicit discovery remains broader, and
unsupported wording can still receive imperfect model suggestions. See [the scope and evidence](../../research/semantic-followup-2026-10-20/lookup-context.md).

### Phrase location and fidelity

Yarn's moved\-phrase check compares a planned spot with one counterpart sentence, preferring its expected
position when lexical scores tie. This prevents nearby sentences from collectively claiming a correctly
placed phrase. Well, the broader verification alignment still permits up to three sentences for splits'n merges.
Both are lexical heuristics; a substantially rewritten sentence may need the writer's explicit review.

Lint compares refrains through the dictionary's drawl annotations. Reviewed whole-phrase `name_aliases` in
`grammar.yaml` can excuse a known capitalised common phrase, such as `Christmas Trees` becoming `Chrissy trees`.
Aliases are explicit: neither `John Woods` nor `Christmas Island` is inferred from its individual words.

## Imagery in plans and lookup

`plan` keeps its `riffs` list: entry\-attached cards retain their existin' fields, while contextual cards add
an image `id`, `concepts`, `frames`, `form`, `subject`, `association`, `exaggeration`, `origin`, `usage` and
`automatic`. Fair dinkum, contextual cards can be offered even where no word substitution was chosen. A direct suffix
can pass automatic insertion checks; rewrite'n related cards always require a writer's judgement.

Full and short entry cards include nonempty `semantic_effects`. Meaning suggestions respect the resolved
`narrator_opinion` permission. Explicit term searches remain discoverable when the effect is disabled,
with `effects_permitted: false` and `effect_rejection`; discovery does not promise that the term can fill a
particular sentence. Plan's selected phrases also carry nonempty effect metadata. Change alternatives share
the translation eligibility check, including alternatives whose vulgarity cap alone is raised.

`lookup` also accepts `embellishment`, `document_type` and `document_config` in Python, CLI and MCP. It adds
an optional `imagery` list when reviewed images match the query, alongside the usual `results`. Image text
and IDs are searchable too. Bare lookup is not a grammatical fit check: its cards have `template: true`,
`automatic: false`, and slots may remain unbound. `short=True` keeps this imagery and its usage conditions.
Session lookup inherits the session's settings. `entry_riffs: false` removes legacy riff cards separately.
See [contextual controls](translation-controls.md#contextual-imagery) before using a suggestion.
